line: Fuel supplier wants cash up front now. Cash. Like we're a fruit stand.
Morning, rookie. Easy one today. Anguilla and back. I'll ride along.
You keep glancing back at the box. It's just a box. Probably nothing.
where: Ch 1 The Extra Box · in flight (climb)

line: Relax, rookie. Land normal, taxi normal, smile at the man. Easy.
where: Ch 1 The Extra Box · in flight (descent)

line: Same friend, one bag, Anguilla to Nevis. Five hundred for you. Don't open it.
Four hundred thousand dollars behind your seat. If anyone stops you, what do you even say?
Coast Guard Dash 8, low level, crossing west of Saba.
The Dash 8 passes high and never looks your way.
where: Ch 2 Cash Run · flight order ok

line: You hesitated. The Dash 8 banks toward you for a closer look, then carries on.
where: Ch 2 Cash Run · flight order fail

line: Nevis traffic, be advised, police vehicle on the apron.
Fish. Just fish. Bring them home and don't stop to chat with anybody.
Slow down, rookie. Customs changes shift at four. Land after that and the new guy waves us through.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (cruise)

line: You land at five past four. The new officer barely looks up.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · flight order ok

line: You land at ten to four. The old officer is still on, and he remembers your face.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · flight order fail

line: Coral Wing, after landing, customs requests you park at the main apron.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (descent)

line: Hangar first. Two minutes. Breathe.
where: Ch 3 The Ramp Check · in flight (final)

line: You must be the pilot Dez keeps telling me about. Calm hands, he says. I'd like to see that.
Be nice to this one, rookie. Real nice.
Castillo hasn't stopped watching your hands on the yoke. You fly like your old instructor is in the right seat.
Show me what my money buys. A steep turn. Forty-five degrees of bank, all the way around.
You roll out on your heading. Castillo nods once. Good.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · flight order ok

line: Castillo watches you wobble through it and says nothing.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · flight order fail

line: Your jet training is paid for. $22,000 is in your account. Book the checkride. Don't make me wait.
where: Ch 4 The Offer · after the flight

line: Lionel Hartwell. My foundation owns her, on paper. Mateo says you're the best he's found.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · prologue

line: Nine bags. Don't count them this time. It's only money, and money isn't a crime until somebody asks where it came from.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · prologue

line: Passing twenty thousand feet in a jet with a million dollars in the back. You wait for the fear. It doesn't come.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (climb)

line: How does she fly? Good. Get used to it. There's a lot more where that came from.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (cruise)

line: Unknown aircraft squawking 4521, say your destination and souls on board.
where: Ch 5 Keys to the Jet · in flight (cruise)

line: No stops. No radio. They paid for a quiet flight.
The boy's breathing is getting louder. Everyone in the back is staring at the back of your head.
The boy is wheezing hard. There's an oxygen bottle in the emergency kit, and Castillo's rule is no stops, no favors.
Arnaud won't stop talking about his daughter. You turn the radio up.
Is my lawyer comfortable? Good. Make sure he gets where he's going.
Arnaud is asleep. His hard drive is sticking out of his jacket pocket.
Nobody else will fly today. That's the point. Name your price, and I'll double it.
You're the pilot? Tico. I load the bags. Someday I'm gonna fly one of these, boss. Watch.
Coast Guard six five zero four, San Juan, returning to base due to weather.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (climb)

line: You're the only plane in the sky. That's why you're worth so much.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (cruise)

line: Rain hammering the windscreen, and you're grinning. When did that start?
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (descent)

line: Punta Cana is reporting a thunderstorm over the field.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · in flight (cruise)

line: The cell drifts off. Late, but every bag is dry.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · flight order ok

line: You landed in the tail of the storm. Two bags are soaked through.
where: Ch 8 Into the Storm · flight order fail

line: Routine run. You're already thinking about what to spend this one on.
There's a sealed case behind your seat and a feeling in your stomach you haven't had since the Cessna days.
You're not a courier anymore. You're part of the machine.
Boss! I'm on your crew now! This is the best day of my whole life.
Fourteen hundred pounds. A 737 freighter carries forty thousand. You do the math again.
A text from an unknown number: We know who you are. You delete it, and then you check your mirrors all the way down.
Nice jet. Where's it going? Text me the tail number of every plane you see on that ramp.
Boss, can I sit up front? Just for a minute? I want to see what it looks like.
Relax, boss. Nobody hits the jet. Who would even try?
Traffic, two o'clock, same altitude, no transponder.
The dark jet can't keep up. It peels off toward the coast.
where: Ch 11 The Medinas · flight order ok

line: They sit on your wing all the way down. Somebody was taking photos.
where: Ch 11 The Medinas · flight order fail

line: Somebody on your crew talks to the DEA. I think it's Tico.
Fly him to Grand Cayman. Someone will meet him there to talk. Just talk.
Boss. You let me sit up front once, remember? Best ten minutes of my life.
where: Ch 12 The Rat · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Tico won't look at you. He rode with you through the storm. He wanted to be a pilot.
Dez knew the risks. My lawyer will ride with you. Don't get sentimental.
Castillo's lawyer finally looks up from Dez's file. How much is Dez worth to you?
Dez won't talk to us. He's protecting someone. If it's you, now would be a good time to tell me.
Dez knew the risks. Don't get sentimental. It's bad for business.
The lawyer works for me, not for Dez. Remember that when she asks you questions.
Don't. Don't explain. Just take me flying. Grand Case, like when you were new.
Mari hasn't said a word since takeoff.
I'll ride in the jump seat, if you don't mind. I have something to give you, and I don't trust phones.
Your first airliner. A hundred and fifty thousand pounds, and every one of them feels like yours.
My foundation has been washing Castillo's money for years. I built it to save a reef. I want out.
If I give you the ledgers, Castillo will know it was me. I'd like a seat on a plane out, after.
Nice airline. I'll take half.
An airline. That's ambitious. Every invoice, every tail number. Send it all to me.
Eighteen tons a night. Your airline. You can't stop smiling.
Half, my friend. We'll talk when you land.
Caribe one, Tocumen ground. Customs requests you taxi to remote stand seven.
My friend! No hard feelings about the airline. I've booked you a run myself. Like old times.
My lawyer tells me you had a lot to say about Dez. Never mind. We're friends.
where: Ch 17 The Setup · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Castillo hasn't been this friendly in months.
Something feels wrong about this one. You can't say what.
Rookie, listen. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. They're waiting on the cargo ramp. Park at the passenger terminal and walk out with the tourists.
Don't park on the cargo ramp. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. Passenger terminal, now.
Our wiretap just lit up. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. Stay off the cargo ramp.
It's Tico. You let me run, so I owe you one. Castillo sold you to the Medinas. They're on the cargo ramp.
Eighty tons, and I tracked every pallet. Bring her home, partner.
Four engines. Eighty tons. Two years ago you were scared of a box in a Cessna.
I hear you're flying a 747 now. Don't forget who taught you.
The trucks are in place. Bring her home, partner.
Heavy aircraft, unidentified, this is the U.S. Coast Guard on guard. Identify yourself.
Down in the radar clutter. The Coast Guard loses you over the water.
They tracked you all the way in.
I'll save you a seat at the table, my friend. Bring the big airplane. They like big airplanes.
A table full of suppliers in Cancún. Tell me you're remembering every face.
Everyone at that table is looking at the sky right now.
Before you land: the suppliers want a show of strength. Do a low pass down the runway. Let them hear four engines.
Four engines at two hundred feet. Every phone at the table is pointed at you.
where: Ch 19 The Table · flight order ok

line: You never got low enough. Medina's men are laughing at the table.
where: Ch 19 The Table · flight order fail

line: I'll ride along, if you don't mind. To make peace.
We're in position. Whatever you're planning, don't.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · prologue (depends on choices)

line: Castillo is pretending to sleep in the jump seat. One hour to Miami. One hour to decide.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · in flight (cruise)

line: We're in position at Miami. Whatever you're planning, don't.
where: Ch 20 The Last Run · in flight (cruise)

line: I don't pay for wreckage. Get yourself together and do it again. Properly.
